title: Space/join MemoryBackend invite lookup is account-scoped; spec semantics are global
description:
Site: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/space.rs:1284-1314 (handle_space_join invite-code path).

In-code acknowledgement (lines 1285-1288): 'NOTE: The MemoryBackend stores objects per-account, so invite code lookup works only when the caller's account created the invite. A production backend must maintain a global invite code index. This is a known architectural limitation of the test backend.'

But the limitation isn't only in MemoryBackend — it's in the handler's API. The handler calls:
    backend.get_objects::<SpaceInvite>(caller, &account_id, None, None)

…and account_id is the redeemer's account. Spec semantics: an invite code is a globally-redeemable handle; any user with the code joins any Space whose invite carries that code, regardless of which JMAP account created the invite.

A production backend that maintains a global invite index can't even *receive* the relevant context here: the trait signature passes account_id, and the handler iterates the result of an account-scoped get_objects.

This is a JmapBackend/ChatBackend trait shape issue, not just a memory.rs limitation: ChatBackend has no method that means 'redeem this invite code from the global index'. Fix sketch:
1. New ChatBackend method: redeem_invite_code(&self, caller, code) -> Result<(account_id, space_id, invite_id), BackendSetError>. The backend resolves which account+space owns the code.
2. handle_space_join's invite branch calls redeem_invite_code; the returned account_id is what the membership write uses (and that may not equal the caller's-supplied accountId).
3. Drop the account_id input from the invite branch path — or treat it as a hint that's ignored.

Without this, the only deployments that work correctly are single-account (every user has their own account that contains everything they care about); multi-tenant or multi-Space-per-account deployments cannot redeem invites that crossed account boundaries.

Note: tests currently mask this because the integration tests create invites and redeem them within the same account. The bug would surface immediately in any deployment with cross-account invite sharing.
notes:
DECISION NEEDED (triage 2026-10-19 at 9fdbbbcf): Question for Mark: which account is an inviteCode resolved in, and does the ChatBackend trait need to change to support that?

Options:
(A) Codes resolve server-wide (the bead's reading). Add a defaulted ChatBackend method, `resolve_invite_code(caller, account_id, code) -> Result<Option<(Id /*hosting account*/, SpaceInvite)>, Error>`. The default keeps today's account-scoped constant-time scan, so the change isn't breaking. A production backend overrides it with a global index. handle_space_join then uses the returned hosting account for the Space fetch, the ban check, and join_space_with_invite. The response's accountId would echo the request. One part stays unsolved: the member entry written into the hosting account would be the joiner's accountId, but §SpaceMember.id requires the joiner's ChatContact.id there. That is the open principal_id family, so this fix depends on it.
(B) Constraint instead of mechanism. Rule that accountId names the account that hosts the Space (RFC 8620 lets a user reach shared accounts), and codes resolve only there. Delete the NOTE, state the rule in the handle_space_join and join_space_with_invite docs, and close the bead as by design. This is size S and not breaking. The cost: someone holding only a code also has to know the hosting accountId.
(C) Clarify the draft first. Add one sentence to draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §Space/join saying whether inviteCode resolution is limited to the request's accountId or covers the whole server. Then implement A or B to match.

My recommendation is C then B. The spec is your own draft, and B removes the whole cross-account category with no new trait surface. Choose A only if cross-account deployments are a goal, and do it together with the principal_id/ChatContact-mapping decision, because without that it writes the wrong member id. For a test oracle, quote the clarified §Space/join sentence. For A, add a two-account MemoryBackend test: create the invite in account X, redeem with account Y, and expect a member added to X's Space with uses = 1.
DECIDED by Mark 2026-10-19: C then B. (1) jmap-chat-spec: add one sentence to draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §Space/join: inviteCode resolves only within the request's accountId, which names the account hosting the Space; invite links therefore carry accountId and code. (2) crate-jmap: delete the 'global invite code index' NOTE in handle_space_join, state the rule in handle_space_join and ChatBackend::join_space_with_invite docs, add a test quoting the new sentence (code from another account -> invalidArguments 'invite code not found'). Non-breaking.
Folded into JMAP-y3f2 (Chat core server conformance (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00)) by the 2026-10-19 spec gap audit. Mark's 2026-10-19 decision (C then B) stands; spec sentence filed as jmap-chat-spec-vvqn.
